questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman being treated for pelvic inflammatory disease should be placed in which position?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's helps localize infection in the pelvis and promotes drainage.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Pelvic inflammatory disease (PDF p. 296)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A serious long-term consequence of pelvic inflammatory disease is:
questions.rationale: Tubal scarring from PID causes ectopic pregnancy, infertility and chronic pelvic pain.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Pelvic inflammatory disease (PDF p. 296)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which instruction is part of discharge teaching for a woman treated for PID?
options: Have her partner examined and treated
Douche daily to clean the vagina
questions.rationale: Treat partners to prevent reinfection; avoid intercourse, tampons and douching for at least a week after therapy.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 PID patient education (PDF p. 296)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman whose periods stopped 3 years ago now has vaginal spotting. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Bleeding 1 year or more after menopause is abnormal and needs evaluation to rule out endometrial cancer.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Abnormal uterine bleeding (PDF p. 296)
questions.quote: Postmenopausal bleeding.Bleeding from the reproductive tract occuming1yearormoreaftermenopause.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding is called:
questions.rationale: Menorrhagia is excessive amount or duration of flow; oligomenorrhea is infrequent; polymenorrhea is too frequent.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Uterine bleeding (PDF p. 296)
questions.quote: Menorhagia (hypermenomhea).Increased amount or duration of menstrualbleeding

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A college student misses classes due to cramping menstrual pain. Which drug is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Primary dysmenorrhea is due to prostaglandins; NSAIDs block prostaglandin synthesis. Oral contraceptives also help.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Dysmenorrhea (PDF p. 297)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 30-year-old has painful periods, pain with intercourse and difficulty conceiving. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Endometrial tissue outside the uterus causes cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, painful defecation and infertility.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Endometriosis (PDF p. 297)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman with large uterine fibroids reports heavy periods with clots and fatigue. The nurse expects which lab finding?
questions.rationale: Leiomyomas cause heavy bleeding; gradual blood loss leads to anemia.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Leiomyomas (PDF p. 298)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A grand multipara feels something "falling out" of her vagina and has stress incontinence. The most common cause of her condition is:
questions.rationale: Uterine prolapse is most often from childbirth trauma; menopause and obesity contribute.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Uterine prolapse (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Most common cause:childbirth trauma like episiotomy extension

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An elderly woman with uterine prolapse is a poor surgical risk. Which option supports the uterus without surgery?
questions.rationale: A pessary is worn in the vagina to support the uterus; Kegel exercises also improve pelvic tone.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Uterine prolapse (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Pessaries:devices wom in the vagina to support the uterus for womenwhoarepoorsurgicalrisks.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Premenstrual syndrome symptoms typically appear:
questions.rationale: PMS occurs in the luteal phase, 7–10 days before menses, and eases with onset of flow.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Premenstrual syndrome (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Symptoms generally appear7 to 10 daysbetore mensesanddecreasn with onset of menses.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which advice helps a woman with premenstrual bloating and irritability?
questions.rationale: Limiting salt, refined sugar, caffeine and animal fat, plus adequate rest, eases PMS.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Premenstrual syndrome (PDF p. 299)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Two long-term health risks after menopause that the nurse should teach about are:
questions.rationale: Loss of estrogen increases bone loss and coronary heart disease risk.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Menopause (PDF p. 299)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A man had a vasectomy last week and asks when he can stop using condoms. The nurse explains:
questions.rationale: Sperm remain in the ducts for a time; unprotected sex is safe only after semen analysis is negative for sperm.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Sterilization (PDF p. 300)
questions.quote: Semen should be negative for sperm,3 times before attemptingunprotected intercourse.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A couple has had regular unprotected intercourse for 14 months without pregnancy. They have had a child before. This is:
questions.rationale: Infertility is failure to conceive after 1 year; it is secondary if there has been a previous pregnancy.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 Infertility (PDF p. 300)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: The most common bacterial STI, often silent in women and a major cause of tubal infertility, is:
questions.rationale: Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial STI and a leading cause of PID and tubal infertility.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Chlamydia (PDF p. 302)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A newborn of a mother with untreated chlamydia is at risk for:
questions.rationale: Passage through an infected birth canal can cause neonatal chlamydial conjunctivitis and pneumonia.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Chlamydia (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: passage through the birth canal of an infected mother can cause conjunctivitis andpneumonia inanewbom.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client treated for gonorrhea is usually also treated for which infection, because they often coexist?
questions.rationale: Gonorrhea and chlamydia frequently occur together, so treatment covers both unless chlamydia is ruled out.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Gonorrhea (PDF p. 303)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A young man has a single painless, firm-edged ulcer on the penis. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: The syphilitic chancre is painless with a raised firm border; chancroid ulcers are painful, herpes forms painful vesicles.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Syphilis (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: A chancre is an oval ulcer witha raised fim borderthatdoesnotbleed readilyand ispainlessunlessinfected

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A non-itchy rash on the palms and soles with mucous patches in the mouth is typical of:
questions.rationale: Secondary syphilis (6–8 weeks after infection) causes a generalized rash on palms and soles that is infectious.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Syphilis (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: appears on the palmsofthe hands and solesofthe feet

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After treatment for primary syphilis, how long should the client avoid sexual contact?
questions.rationale: Clients with primary or secondary syphilis should abstain for at least 1 month after treatment, and partners must be evaluated.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Syphilis treatment (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: Clients with primary or secondary syphilis should abstain fromsexual contactforatleast1month aftertreatment.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Why is syphilis screening important in every pregnant woman?
options: It can cross the placenta at any stage
It cannot be treated in pregnancy
questions.rationale: Untreated syphilis passes to the fetus transplacentally (congenital syphilis); penicillin treats both.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Syphilis (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: The infection can also be passed transplacentally from an untreated pregnant woman to herfetus during ary stage of the disease

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman in labor has active genital herpes lesions. The nurse anticipates:
questions.rationale: Newborns can be infected during vaginal birth when lesions are active; cesarean section prevents this.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Genital herpes (PDF p. 304)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client with recurrent genital herpes asks if he can have sex safely when no sores are present. The nurse explains:
options: Use condoms; spread can occur without sores
Herpes is cured after the first attack
questions.rationale: Herpes is a lifelong infection; viral shedding can occur without lesions, so condoms are advised.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Genital herpes (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: The possible nisk of transmission existsevenwhenlesionsarenotpresent

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Multiple painful, deep genital ulcers with tender swollen inguinal nodes suggest:
questions.rationale: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) causes painful ulcers and tender adenopathy; test also for HIV and syphilis.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Chancroid (PDF p. 304)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Genital warts are caused by a virus strongly linked with:
questions.rationale: Human papillomavirus causes condylomata acuminata and is strongly associated with cervical and penile cancer; HPV vaccine prevents it.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 Genital warts (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: t is strongly associatedwith carcinoma of the genitals,including the cervixandpenis.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client on metronidazole should be told to avoid:
questions.rationale: Alcohol with metronidazole causes a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, vomiting).
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 20 HIV-related drugs (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: Avoid alcohol during treatment toprevent disulfiram- likemanifestations.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which immunoglobulin crosses the placenta and protects the newborn?
questions.rationale: IgG is the most abundant antibody and the only one that crosses the placenta.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Immunoglobulins (PDF p. 307)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Breastfed infants get protection against intestinal infections mainly from which antibody in colostrum?
questions.rationale: Secretory IgA is found in colostrum, saliva, tears and mucus and protects mucosal surfaces.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Immunoglobulins (PDF p. 307)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn with absent thymus has tetany from low calcium. This suggests:
questions.rationale: DiGeorge syndrome (thymic hypoplasia) causes T-cell deficiency and hypocalcemia from hypoparathyroidism.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Primary immunodeficiencies (PDF p. 308)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client stung by a bee develops wheezing, hives and hypotension. The first drug the nurse expects to give is:
questions.rationale: Anaphylaxis (type I) is treated first with epinephrine; antihistamines and steroids follow.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Type I hypersensitivity (PDF p. 309)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A hemolytic reaction from ABO-incompatible blood is which type of hypersensitivity?
questions.rationale: Type II reactions involve antibodies against cell surfaces, as in ABO incompatibility and drug-induced hemolysis.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Hypersensitivity (PDF p. 309)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A positive tuberculin skin test read after 48–72 hours is an example of which hypersensitivity?
questions.rationale: Type IV reactions are T-cell mediated and delayed: TB skin test, contact dermatitis, transplant rejection.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Hypersensitivity (PDF p. 309)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An older client has bone pain, fractures, anemia and high serum calcium. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Multiple myeloma, a plasma cell cancer, causes widespread bone destruction, anemia and hypercalcemia.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 21 Gammopathies (PDF p. 308)
